intro.name: Krish Vedak
intro.tagline: Thinking about how silicon turns ideas into computation.
bio: Hi, I'm Krish. I study computer architecture and VLSI design, and I'm curious about what happens between a line of code and the transistors that run it.
This site is my notebook: what I'm interested in, what I've learned, what I've built, and things I write to understand them better.

interests.title: Processor microarchitecture
interests.text: Pipelines, out-of-order execution, branch prediction and the trade-offs behind them.

interests.title: Digital VLSI design
interests.text: RTL to layout: synthesis, timing closure, and physical design flows.

interests.title: Memory systems
interests.text: Caches, coherence and bandwidth, where performance is often won or lost.

interests.title: Low-power design
interests.text: Making circuits efficient through clock gating, voltage scaling and smarter design choices.

interests.title: Hardware accelerators
interests.text: Domain-specific designs for machine learning and signal processing.

interests.title: Open-source hardware
interests.text: RISC-V and open EDA tools that make chip design more accessible.

projects.title: 5-stage RISC-V pipelined core
projects.text: A pipelined RV32I processor in Verilog with hazard detection and forwarding, verified with a self-checking testbench.

projects.title: Cache simulator
projects.text: A configurable set-associative cache simulator for comparing replacement policies across memory traces.

projects.title: Inverter chain layout
projects.text: Designed and simulated an inverter chain, characterising delay and power across process corners.

points: Wrote and verified RTL for a small peripheral block.
Cut simulation runtime by improving the regression setup.
Documented the block for the wider team.
